title: The one line, and why plans must bend
objectives: Use the one line in any withdrawal conversation.
Explain why a rigid plan breaks and a flexible one lasts.
body_md:
The one line to remember: spend from safety, grow from equity, and refill on a plan. A rigid plan breaks in a bad year: fixed withdrawals from falling equity, inflation increases regardless of the corpus, big costs paid from the monthly SWP. A flexible plan bends: skip the inflation increase, draw from Bucket 2, fund big costs from their own pot, and rebuild over time. Flexible spending in bad years is one of the most powerful ways to make a corpus last.

> **Investor takeaway:** Spend from safety, grow from equity, and refill on a plan.
example: Bad year, fixed plan: sell equity low to pay bills. Flexible plan: Bucket 2 pays, equity recovers, inflation increase skipped.
say: Flexible spending in bad years is one of the most powerful ways to make a corpus last.
A rigid plan breaks; a flexible plan bends.
